summary: Karl Schenkl was a scholar in linguistics, Indology, and other fields. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Vienna (1845–1849) and studied under Georg Curtius (~1849–1851), later holding professorships at Innsbruck (1857–1864), Graz (1864–1875), and Vienna (1875–1899).

Karl Schönfeld was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Neuchâtel, Göttingen under Franz Kielhorn (1898–1900), and Zurich under Adolf Kaegi (1900–1910, Ph.D.). He served as a teacher at Kantonsschule Rychenberg from 1905 to 1928.

Karl Scriba, who worked in Indology and linguistics, studied at the University of Munich, Humboldt University of Berlin, and the University of Würzburg, where he earned his PhD under doctoral supervisor Julius Jolly in 1902.

Karl Verner was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Copenhagen (Mag. 1864–1873) under Niels Ludvig Westergaard, and under August Leskien (~1871–1872). He served as a librarian in Halle-Wittenberg before becoming a Docent in Copenhagen in 1882.

Karl Vilhelm Zetterstéen was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He completed his Ph.D. at Uppsala University under Herman Almkvist and Eduard Sachau, later serving as Docent at Uppsala (1895) and Lund (1895–1904), and Professor at Uppsala (1904–1931).

Karl von Hegel was a historian and archaeologist. He held academic posts at the University of Rostock from around 1841 to 1856 and at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg from approximately 1856 to 1893.

Karl-Heinz Brodbeck is a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees from Augsburg and the University of Munich (PhD ~1974–1981). He held positions at Munich (1978–1988) and was a professor at the Technical University of Applied Sciences Würzburg-Schweinfurt (1992–2014).

Karl-Heinz Everding is a Tibetologist who earned his PhD from the University of Bonn (~1980–1985) and completed his Habilitation at Hamburg in 1999. He worked at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (~1993–2018) and taught at Hamburg.
Karl-Heinz Gottmann was a scholar in Buddhist studies. He was the primary student of Anagarika Govinda, studying under him from around 1952 to 1985, and succeeded him in 1982.

Karl-Stéphan Bouthillette is an Indologist, philosopher, and Buddhist studies scholar. He lectured at the University of Munich (2015–2019), Laval University (2019–2020), held a post-doc at FWO (2019–2022), and held assistant professorships at MAHE (2023) and the University of Hong Kong (2026).
Karma Lek Shé Drayang was an individual who studied under the Buddhist masters Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.

Karma Lekshe Tsomo is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied at UC Berkeley, UH Mānoa, and under the 14th Dalai Lama. She served as Assistant Professor at the University of San Diego (2000–2022) and Numata Professor at UH Mānoa (2023).

Karma Phuntsho is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He completed his D.Phil. at Oxford under Michael Aris and Richard Gombrich, held a post-doc at CNRS, and served as a research associate at Cambridge (~2003–2009).

Karma Sonam Palmo works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. She earned Shastri and Acharya degrees at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and completed a Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Tasmania under Lucy Tatman and Sonam Thakchoe.

Karma Thinley Rinpoche is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies teacher. He served as abbot of the Young Lamas Home School around 1962 and the Karma Drubgyu Thargay Ling Nunnery, and founded Kampo Gangra Drubgyud Ling and Tekchen Lekshay Ling.

Karma Ura is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Tibetology. He completed studies at St. Stephen's College, Magdalen College, Oxford, and the University of Edinburgh, and served as Director of the Centre for Bhutan Studies and GNH from 1999 to 2008.
Karmen Bašić was an Indologist who studied at the University of Zagreb from around 1961 to 1966. She later served as Executive Director of the Open Society Institute Croatia from around 1993 to 1999.

Karsé Kongtrul studied under the 13th Dalai Lama, Khakyab Dorje, Shechen Gyaltsab, and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö. He also taught Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and Khenpo Gangshar.

Karthigesu Indrapala is a historian, archaeologist, and Indologist who studied at Jaffna College, the University of Ceylon, and under Arthur Llewellyn Basham (~1962–1965). He later held an academic post at the University of Tokyo.

Karuna Kusalasaya was a scholar of Indology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He held posts as a research scholar and Assistant to the Director at Visva-Bharati University and as Professor of Sanskrit at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University.
